title: Apple Is Hiring to Build Its Own Computer-Use AI Agent
dek: A new job post describes an agent that browses, codes and runs apps.

facts.label: Date the Cupertino job listing was posted
Top of the role's base pay range
Apple Foundation Models team is a partner

caption:
Apple just revealed its next big AI move, and it wasn't in a keynote. It was in a job listing. 👀

A new post for a "Senior Engineering Manager, Agentic AI – Proactive" in Cupertino describes an Apple AI agent that uses a computer like a person: browsing the web, working across apps, running terminal commands, writing and debugging code, and calling APIs. The team will partner with Siri, UI frameworks and Apple Foundation Models, with a focus on on-device models, sandboxing and strict permissions.

Why it matters: ChatGPT, Perplexity, Meta's Muse and now Gemini can already control the Mac, while Apple has no agent of its own. The word "Proactive" hints at a Siri that acts before you ask. No name, devices or launch date yet, so treat it as an early signal.

We're tracking every step of the AI agent race at AI Parabellum. Would you trust an agent to run your Mac?

post_caption:
Apple doesn't have an AI agent yet, but its careers page says one is on the way.

The listing outlines a privacy-first agent that plans multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, code and the command line, built with Siri and Apple's on-device models. Nothing is announced, but the race with ChatGPT and Gemini on the Mac just got more interesting. 🍎
